visual.general_description: Grayscale axial cross-sectional pelvic image with two red arrow outlines.
visual.detailed_description: Grayscale axial cross-sectional image of the pelvis. The bony pelvis is bright white at the left, right and lower center, with a rounded, brighter, mottled soft-tissue structure at the center. Large uniform mid-gray areas lie in the upper left and upper right of the image beneath a dark band at the top edge. Two red hollow arrow outlines are drawn on the image: one in the upper left pointing toward the image center and one in the upper right pointing toward the image center, each next to a mid-gray area. A thin dotted curved line runs along the right edge and a straight white line crosses the lower right corner. No printed text, letters, numbers, scale bar or labels are visible.

Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis (CTAP) was done in the ED and showed large-volume hemoperitoneum, with the likely source being a ruptured right corpus luteal cyst (Figure 1).
